summary.text: Soil microbiology is the study of microorganisms in soil, their functions, and how they affect soil properties.
Soil microorganisms include bacteria, archaea, fungi, algae, slime molds and protozoa, with bacteria and archaea the most abundant.
Bacteria fix nitrogen into forms plants can use, and fungi break down plant debris and help soil particles bind into aggregates.

facts.label: Root zone count
facts.value: Up to 10 billion culturable bacterial cells per gram

facts.label: Sugar beet survey
facts.value: In 2011, over 33,000 bacterial and archaeal species on roots

facts.label: Limiting nutrient
facts.value: Nitrogen is often the most limiting in soil and water

facts.label: Antibiotic makers
facts.value: Actinomycetes, source of streptomycin and erythromycin

facts.label: Rhizosphere
facts.value: The region around plant roots, a hotspot of microbial diversity

items.prompt: Crops stall for lack of the nutrient most often scarce in soil and water. How do bacteria help?

options.label: They pull the nutrient out of the rock by weathering minerals alone
They turn atmospheric nitrogen into compounds such as ammonia that plants can use
They store it as spores until the plant dies
They stop other microbes from using up the water

items.explain: Nitrogen is often the most limiting nutrient, and bacteria fix atmospheric dinitrogen into compounds such as ammonia that plants can use.

items.prompt: Most bacteria in soil away from plant roots are inactive. What could rouse them?

options.label: Sugary exudates from a growing root tip
A further spell of drying out
Being ground into a finer powder

items.explain: Bulk-soil bacteria stay quiescent until reached by exudates from growing root tips or the mucus of burrowing earthworms.

items.prompt: A microbe in a flask grows in distinct clumps, forms spores and branches like a fungus, yet is a bacterium. What is it likely?
items.explain: Actinomycetes are bacteria that share shape, branching, spore formation and clumped growth in liquid culture with fungi.

items.prompt: One soil genus handles many chemicals, while another can gain energy in only one way. Which is the narrow one?
items.explain: Nitrobacter can only derive energy by oxidizing nitrite to nitrate, while Pseudomonas can metabolize a wide range of chemicals.

items.prompt: Soil archaea are still poorly known. Which two processes might they play a significant role in?
items.explain: Soil archaea could play a significant role in nitrification and methanogenesis.

items.prompt: Counting cells, bacteria beat fungi in a soil sample. Why might fungi still matter more by other measures?

options.label: Each fungal cell fixes more nitrogen than a bacterium
They make nearly all the soil's antibiotics
In some soils they contribute greater biomass and respiration
They live only in the root zone, so they get counted twice

items.explain: Fungi may be outnumbered in cell counts but can contribute greater biomass and respiration rate in some soil types.
